raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Sparse-prefill scratch replacement allocates its new tensor while the backend still owns the old one. A larger workspace (or a different dtype) can therefore fail even when the replacement alone fits the available allocator budget.

This is a follow-up to #43921, which left workspace retention unchanged. The release-before-replacement change was originally proposed by @divyvasal  in #43726. Refs #41076; this addresses the transient replacement peak, not the independently unbounded size of a batch of long histories.

## Modifications

Release the workspace owner's old tensor reference before allocating a replacement. Scratch contents are overwritten by the existing caller. Requests that fit the current capacity still reuse the buffer, and views retained by a caller continue owning their original storage.

Add a single-GPU regression with fresh subprocesses so the allocator cap cannot affect other tests or a resident server.

## Accuracy Tests

On an H200 with Torch 2.14.1+cu130, starting from upstream `a3abea35609eeeff7e165486dd614963af211161`:

```bash
python test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_sparse_prefill_workspace.py -v
```

| Isolated 128 MiB allocator limit | Unmodified main | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grow 64 MiB BF16 scratch to 96 MiB | OOM | Pass |
| Replace 48 MiB byte scratch with 96 MiB BF16 scratch | OOM | Pass |
| Retained-view values and smaller-request reuse | Pass | Pass |

Both replacement cases pass the below-100-MiB peak-allocation assertion after the fix. These are controlled allocator regressions using the actual workspace class, not a replay of the reported production OOM. No model weights or full serving workload are used.

Existing DSV4 compressed sparse-prefill attention (C4/C128) and workspace reuse tests also pass on H200. The initial numerical-test attempt failed to link `libcudart` with the pip CUDA path; using the complete `/usr/local/cuda-13.0` toolkit passed without source changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel, gather layout or attention math changes. No throughput claim; the measured improvement is successful scratch replacement under the same allocator cap.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] CUDA regression fails on unmodified main and passes after the fix.
- [x] Retained views and existing capacity reuse remain valid.
- [ ] Upstream GPU CI and maintainer review.

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+"""Sparse-prefill scratch replacement must fit without retaining its old owner.
+
+The allocator limit belongs to a fresh subprocess, so it cannot affect other
+CUDA tests or a serving process sharing the device.
+"""
+
+import json
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=20, stage="base-b", runner_config="1-gpu-small")
+
+_RESIZE_PROBE = """
+import json
+import sys
+import torch
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsv4.sparse_prefill_utils import SparsePrefillWorkspace
+
+case = sys.argv[1]
+device = torch.device("cuda:0")
+limit = 128 * 1024**2
+torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(
+    limit / torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).total_memory, device
+)
+torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(device)
+assert base < 8 * 1024**2, base
+torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(device)
+workspace = SparsePrefillWorkspace(device)
+if case == "growth":
+    workspace.get(64 * 1024).fill_(1)
+else:
+    workspace.get(96 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8).fill_(1)
+# Each new allocation is 96 MiB. Holding the old storage would exceed 128 MiB.
+result = workspace.get(96 * 1024)
+result.fill_(2)
+assert result.shape == (96 * 1024, 1, 512)
+assert result.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+assert result[0, 0, 0].item() == result[-1, 0, -1].item() == 2
+peak = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(device) - base
+assert peak <= 100 * 1024**2, peak
+print(json.dumps({"case": case, "peak_bytes": peak, "limit_bytes": limit}))
+"""
+
+
+class TestSparsePrefillWorkspace(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_replacement_fits_without_old_scratch(self):
+        """A larger scratch buffer fits, although old plus new would not."""
+        for case in ("growth", "dtype"):
+            with self.subTest(case=case):
+                completed = subprocess.run(
+                    [sys.executable, "-c", _RESIZE_PROBE, case],
+                    check=False,
+                    capture_output=True,
+                    text=True,
+                    timeout=60,
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    completed.returncode, 0, completed.stdout + completed.stderr
+                )
+                result = json.loads(completed.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
+                self.assertLess(result["peak_bytes"], result["limit_bytes"])
+
+    def test_live_views_and_reuse(self):
+        """Replacing the owner must preserve views held by an existing caller."""
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dsv4.sparse_prefill_utils import (
+            SparsePrefillWorkspace,
+        )
+
+        workspace = SparsePrefillWorkspace(torch.device("cuda:0"))
+        old_view = workspace.get(32)
+        old_view.fill_(1)
+        new_view = workspace.get(64)
+        new_view.fill_(2)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(old_view, torch.ones_like(old_view))
+        torch.testing.assert_close(new_view, torch.full_like(new_view, 2))
+        smaller_view = workspace.get(16)
+        self.assertEqual(smaller_view.data_ptr(), new_view.data_ptr())
+        torch.testing.assert_close(smaller_view, new_view[:16])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
